title: SpaceXAI Deploys 420,000 Nvidia GPUs in November to Meet Billions in Commitments

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The AI unit of SpaceX is rushing to fulfill extensive compute obligations by activating a massive fleet of hardware in the coming weeks. According to The Information, the company plans to bring roughly 420,000 Nvidia GPUs online in November to satisfy agreements worth billions of dollars, a target that exceeds previous estimates of 220,000 units for the month.

This acceleration is part of a broader rollout of the Colossus 1 and 2 clusters, which could reach a total of 1.44 million GPUs by year-end. Elon Musk's previously disclosed schedule includes 220,000 GB300 chips coming operational this week and another batch in December. While analysts project total server power will reach 2.7 GW by the end of the year, some critics argue currently operational capacity is only 1 GW. The investment for GPUs in the fourth quarter alone is estimated at over $50 billion.

selectedTweets.text:
Yesterday, Elon posted some details about SpaceX's GPU fleet.

Let's analyze.

According to Elon, Colossus 1 includes 150K H100s, 50K H200s, and 30K GB200s. In Colossus 2, GB200s make up one fifth of the fleet and GB300s the rest (110K GB200s and 440K GB300s).

If we use SpaceX's own definition of "GW," which counts GPU power alone, simple math gets us to roughly 1GW.

In other words, while SpaceX claimed in its latest 10-Q to have deployed an additional 0.4GW, that capacity was not operational or online.

But SpaceX still counts it as deployed GW. Of course.

Now, of the GB300s, 220K will hopefully, finally, be operational next week, a full quarter or more later. Simple math puts that at just over 0.3GW. If we're generous, as generous as SpaceX is with its disclosures, let's call it 0.4GW: the same 0.4GW SpaceX claimed to have deployed in Q2, which, as Elon just revealed, is only becoming operational a quarter later.

None of what Elon said is new to us. I detailed all of this in my article on SpaceX.

selectedTweets.bestBit: implies ~2.7 GW of server power (~3+ GW facility) by year-end
selectedTweets.text:
Elon’s latest GPU schedule here implies ~2.7 GW of server power (~3+ GW facility) by year-end if the December tranche arrives on time & online vs. his comments on SpaceX’s August expectation of “over 2 GW" back in August.

The math, using its filing’s initial cluster figures:
>GB200: 210 MW ÷ 110k GPUs = 1.91 kW/GPU
>GB300: 220 MW ÷ 110k GPUs = 2.00 kW/GPU
>December: 110k GB200 × 1.91 kW + 1.10M GB300 × 2.00 kW + ~300 MW estimated for Colossus 1 = ~2.7 GW

That puts combined server power at ~1.4 GW now, ~1.8 GW next week and ~2.3 GW in November. +Epoch’s 14% allowance for other IT equipment takes December to ~3.1 GW IT, before cooling and facility losses.

This schedule suggests upside to the earlier outlooks.
